Design decisions: computeConvexHull uses deterministic Andrew monotone chain (lexicographic sort by x then y, duplicate points removed, collinear points dropped via <=0 pop, CCW winding, returns hull vertex count, at most `count`); n<3 after dedupe copies the surviving points straight through. computePolygonCenter uses cpCentroidForPoly for count>=3 with non-zero area, midpoint for count==2, and falls back to the vertex average for zero-area/degenerate outlines (cpCentroidForPoly divides by the signed area sum and would produce inf/NaN there). isPolygonConvex returns false for count<3 and for fully collinear input. segmentIntersect rejects |r x s| < 1e-6 (covers parallel and zero-length input) and requires both t and u in [0,1]. Epsilon is a file-local anonymous-namespace constant kHelperEpsilon = 1e-6f. Added <algorithm> and <vector> includes; left the pre-existing <cstring> include in place although it is now unused.

All 30 declared methods implemented (ctor/dtor left as-is). Proven from in-tree call sites: cpArbiterGetShapes/CP_ARBITER_GET_SHAPES, cpShapeGetUserData, cpShapeGetBody, cpShapeGetSensor (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp), cpArbiterGet/SetRestitution, cpArbiterGet/SetFriction, cpArbiterGet/SetSurfaceVelocity, cpArbiterIgnore (CCPhysicsContact.cpp), cpBodyGetVelocityAtWorldPoint(body, cpVect) (CCPhysicsBody.cpp:508). The 9 listed identifiers are standard Chipmunk 7 public arbiter API but have no in-tree call site and external/ is not vendored, so they could not be verified against a header - worth a grep against the real chipmunk.h. Deliberate design decisions a reviewer should confirm: (1) per-point normalImpulse/tangentImpulse are the arbiter total impulse projected on normal/tangent divided evenly by contact count, because Chipmunk 7 exposes no public per-contact-point impulse accessor (jnAcc/jtAcc live in the private cpContact struct, and I avoided chipmunk_private.h and guessing struct fields). (2) getTotalNormalImpulse/getTotalTangentImpulse return std::fabs of the projection (magnitudes) - cpArbiterTotalImpulse is sign-flipped depending on arb->swapped, so a raw projection would usually be negative. getTotalImpulse still returns the signed vector. (3) CollisionPoint::depth stores the raw cpArbiterGetDepth value (Chipmunk reports penetration as negative); computeOverlap reports max std::fabs(depth) so it is positive and sign-convention agnostic. (4) computeRelativeVelocity = velocityB - velocityA at computeContactCenter(), so computeSeparatingVelocity is positive when separating given the Chipmunk normal points from shape A to shape B. (5) computeContactCenter averages the midpoint of pointA/pointB per contact. (6) getContactPoints writes getContactCount() entries and reports 0 in *outCount when outPoints is null (there is no capacity parameter in the header signature, so the caller must supply room for getContactCount() points; Chipmunk caps this at CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER). (7) update() delegates to init() and calls invalidate() on failure; invalidate() drops only _arbiter and _valid (shapes are retained but every accessor gates on _arbiter != nullptr and _valid). No new #includes were added; <cmath> was already present for std::fabs, matching the std::fabs style used in CCPhysicsHelper.cpp. Note CCPhysicsHelper.cpp (cpv2point/point2cpv/cpfloat2float) is being implemented concurrently by another agent - this file depends on those being correct.

Chipmunk headers are not vendored anywhere in the tree (external/ only has config.json), so cpArbiterGetContactPointSet / cpContactPointSet field names could not be read from a header. I used the Chipmunk 7 layout (int count; cpVect normal; struct { cpVect pointA, pointB; cpFloat distance; } points[]), which matches both the stated API version and this tree's own CollisionPoint struct in CCPhysicsCollisionPair.h (pointA/pointB). If Chipmunk 6.2 were in play the field would be points[i].point instead - worth a double check. Everything else was proven from headers in the tree: PhysicsHelper::cpv2point (CCPhysicsHelper.h), PhysicsContactData::POINT_MAX/points/count/normal and the EventCode enum plus the friend declaration granting access to _contactInfo and generateContactData (CCPhysicsContact.h), PhysicsShape::getGroup() (CCPhysicsShape.h line 337, reached via CCPhysicsBody.h). No new #includes were needed. Two intentional deviations from a literal upstream copy: (1) generateContactData clamps count to POINT_MAX before filling points[] (harmless - CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER is 2 in Chipmunk 7, so the clamp never triggers, but it guarantees count never exceeds the array); (2) POSTSOLVE deliberately does NOT call generateContactData, matching upstream. onEvent still leaves _result untouched for POSTSOLVE/SEPARATE, as upstream does, so PhysicsWorld::resetResult keeps its prior value semantics. Only this one .cpp was modified.

Implemented/fixed: addShape, setMass, addMass, addMoment, beforeSimulation, afterSimulation, onAdd, addToPhysicsWorld, removeFromPhysicsWorld. onEnter/onExit were already correct and left byte-identical.

Reviewer should double check three deliberate judgement calls:

1) addShape does NOT wrap addMass/addMoment in an explicit `!= PHYSICS_INFINITY` guard (the assignment text suggested one). The sentinel is handled inside addMass/addMoment. A guard there would be a behavioural regression: CCPhysicsShape.cpp sets _mass=_moment=PHYSICS_INFINITY for all edge shapes (lines 439-440, 736-737, 787-788, 882-883), and CCPhysicsBody.h line 61 documents "If you create body with createEdgeXXX, the mass and moment will be PHYSICS_INFINITY by default". With a guard, edge bodies would report mass 1.0 (MASS_DEFAULT) instead.

2) addShape guards the world registration with `if (_world != nullptr)` only. PhysicsWorld::addBody uses addBodyOrDelay, so a body can have _world set while its cpBody is not yet in the cpSpace; cpSpaceAddShape asserts that the shape's body is already in the space. This mirrors upstream, but a stricter guard (cpSpaceContainsBody(_world->_cpSpace, _cpBody), both accessible since PhysicsBody is a friend of PhysicsWorld) would be safer if that assert is ever hit. Cannot be verified here since external/chipmunk is not vendored.

3) addToPhysicsWorld has an extra null check on scene->getPhysicsWorld() (upstream dereferences it unguarded). Semantically identical when the scene has a physics world; only avoids a null deref for a PhysicsBody attached to a non-physics Scene.

Left intentionally untouched (not hollowed, outside the three assigned items, and no marker/placeholder in them): removeShape and removeAllShapes still adjust _mass/_moment with std::max(0.0f, _mass - shape->getMass()) instead of addMass/addMoment, so they neither honour the PHYSICS_INFINITY sentinel nor sync the cpBody, and they do not call _world->removeShape(). That is an asymmetry with the now-correct addShape. Fixing it requires care: PhysicsShape::setBody re-enters PhysicsBody::removeShape, which is why this tree sets shape->_body = nullptr before setBody(nullptr); and PhysicsWorld::removeShape is itself a no-op stub in the file assigned to another agent.

No new includes were added; no headers or other files modified. Brace count balanced (161/161), zero "Hollowed in benchmark base" occurrences, no (void)param casts left over and no unused parameters (parentToWorldTransform and nodeToWorldTransform are both genuinely used now).
